---
title: "estiMINT: EIR and HBR"
---

`estimint` supplies the entomological inoculation rate (EIR) that every model downstream needs,
inverting either a parasite prevalence or a human biting rate (HBR) into the EIR that would
sustain it, and converting between EIR and HBR in both directions. What comes back is always a
single equilibrium value rather than a trajectory, because the trajectories come from
[stateMINT](../05-statemint/index.qmd). That distinction is set out in
[EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases](../03-concepts/equilibrium.qmd).

::: {.chapter-outline}
- [Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd)
    - A net mix and a resistance level become the two numbers the models consume.
- [Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd)
    - The core inversion, and the reason a lookup table will not do.
- [EIR and HBR](eir-and-hbr.qmd)
    - The other two models, and the error a round trip through both accumulates.
- [Mosquito density and EIR](mosquito-density.qmd)
    - The effect of larviciding, or of a wetter climate, on transmission.
- [estiMINT API](api.qmd)
    - The inference surface, function by function.
:::

## The three models

`estimint` ships three gradient-boosted models inside the wheel, each mapping one driving input
to one output while holding the same six covariates fixed. Nothing is downloaded. Pick the model
whose driving input you measured.

| Model name | Driving input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `"prevalence"` | `prev_y9` (parasite prevalence) | EIR |
| `"eir_to_hbr"` | `eir` | HBR |
| `"hbr"` | `hbr_y9` (human biting rate) | EIR |

Each model is named for its *input*, so the model named `"hbr"` takes an HBR and returns an EIR.

All three are loaded by name with `load_xgb_model` and called with `run_xgb_model`, and the six
shared covariates (`dn0_use`, `Q0`, `phi_bednets`, `seasonal`, `itn_use` and `irs_use`) describe
the setting, though two of them are not survey quantities at all and come out of `calculate_dn0`
instead. Most errors made with the package start there. Please see
[Nets and dn0](nets-and-dn0.qmd) for that calculation.
